passages: September 8, 2026. James Strahler II was sentenced to 180 months in prison.
Strahler pleaded guilty in April to cyberstalking, producing obscene visual representations of child sexual abuse and publication of digital forgeries.

His conviction of publication of digital forgeries is part of the Take It Down Act, a law enacted in 2025 that prohibits non-consensual online publication of intimate visual depictions and AI forgeries.
The conduct involved real and AI-generated images, harassment and threats to adult women and children.

records.authority: Primary current consumer removal and reporting guidance
passages: Image-based abuse includes real, digitally altered and AI-generated intimate images shared without consent.
Certain platforms must provide a removal request process and remove the image and known identical copies within 48 hours.
Report a platform to TakeItDown.ftc.gov if it fails to remove the image or has no working removal process.
The FTC directs reports about perpetrators to local criminal law enforcement and the FBI.
records.limitation: United States legal framework; covered platforms and valid request conditions apply; not a promise of worldwide erasure.
